page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.r5.xlarge is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance deployed on the KVM hypervisor. Hardware resources include an Intel Xeon 8163 processor clocked at 2.5 GHz, utilizing the x86_64 architecture with support for AVX, AVX-512, and AES instructions. The instance provisions 4 dedicated virtual CPUs derived from 2 physical cores utilizing two threads per core. System memory totals 32 GB, yielding an 8 GB per vCPU ratio that defines its memory-heavy resource profile. The configuration contains no local NVMe or SSD storage and includes a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

Synthetic and practical benchmark results place the computing performance of ecs.r5.xlarge in the lower tiers. The instance achieved a Geekbench single-core score of 1005.0 and a multi-core score of 2214.0, while PassMark overall CPU scoring registered at 3635.88. Both single-core and multi-core stress-ng tests placed the machine within the lower 25 percent performance category. Memory bandwidth tests indicated 164.23 GB/sec for small cached blocks, declining to 20.9 GB/sec for large uncached read operations. Database operations scored 1105.52 on PassMark, while Redis SET throughput measured 2.85 million operations per second.

The primary tradeoff of the ecs.r5.xlarge lies in its pairing of generous RAM capacity with conservative processor and memory throughput. With an 8:1 memory-to-core ratio, it offers qualitative resource efficiency for setups where operating footprints require substantial memory tables without consuming high CPU cycles. However, the lack of local storage requires reliance on network-attached block devices, which interact with the 2 Gbps network baseline. As a result, this instance is appropriate for memory-resident caching tiers, Redis instances, intermediate ETL staging, and database workloads requiring memory density over rapid computational throughput.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.r5.xlarge is a memory-optimized virtual server powered by Intel Xeon 8163 processors running at 2.5 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The instance provides 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 2 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, alongside 32 GB of system memory. This configuration establishes an 8 GB memory-to-vCPU ratio. The virtual machine includes no bundled local storage and features a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps, requiring network-attached storage for persistent disk operations. Benchmark evaluations place both single-thread and multi-thread CPU throughput in the lower quartile, alongside subdued uncached memory bandwidth scores. Because compute performance is constrained relative to modern platforms, this instance prioritizes memory capacity over raw processing power. The ecs.r5.xlarge is best matched to memory-bound workloads that do not demand heavy continuous CPU execution, such as Redis caching layers, medium-scale in-memory datastores, and memory-intensive enterprise application tiers.
